key_reasoning.reason: Touches 5 components across 3 layers: the shared codemie_tools base models (CredentialTypes/ToolSet enums), a new ms_exchange package (ExchangeToolConfig with a dual-path auth validator, plus an autodiscovered no-tool ExchangeToolkit), the settings service (secret encryption and masking), the customer-config declarations service (default-off features:exchangePolling), and an alembic migration. Editing the shared base enums is already reflected in the L score, so no separate bump was applied.

The diffstat shows 13 files (774 insertions, 1 deletion), which maps to XL (11-15). About 4 files were modified: the guide, customer_config_declarations.py, settings.py and base/models.py. About 9 are new: 3 ms_exchange source files, 1 migration and 5 test files, spread over src/codemie, src/codemie_tools, src/external, tests and .ai-run. More than half the new files are tests, so the XL file count overstates the implementation effort.

Touches the Service layer (settings and customer-config), the DB-Persistence layer (a reversible credentialtypes enum migration using sync_enum_values, whose downgrade deletes MS_EXCHANGE settings rows) and the tool/integration config layer. No API, UI or live External protocol code is included. Because persistence includes a schema (enum) change, this scores L.

The closest pattern is the existing credential-type additions (the MS_TEAMS enum migration and the sensitive-field config models). It covers the security-sensitive parts: secrets are marked json_schema_extra sensitive and go through the existing settings encryption and masking. So there is no divergence bump. The validator is a small, deterministic required-fields check for each auth path. The migration is reversible.

The total of 20 sits at the M/L boundary. The bundled L example epmcdme-10401 (22, also with a schema migration and credential storage) is close. This change scores lower on clarity and risk because the requirements were fully specified and the precedent pattern covers the work. Tie-break rule: Technical Risk is M and existing patterns cover more than half the implementation, so the score leans lower and stays M.
